name: VALUE
description: Most existing video-and-language (VidL) research focuses on a single dataset, or multiple datasets of a single task. In reality, a truly useful VidL system is expected to be easily generalizable to diverse tasks, domains, and datasets. To facilitate the evaluation of such systems, we introduce Video-And-Language Understanding Evaluation (VALUE) benchmark, an assemblage of 11 VidL datasets over 3 popular tasks: (i) text-to-video retrieval; (ii) video question answering; and (iii) video captioning. VALUE benchmark aims to cover a broad range of video genres, video lengths, data volumes, and task difficulty levels. Rather than focusing on single-channel videos with visual information only, VALUE promotes models that leverage information from both video frames and their associated subtitles, as well as models that share knowledge across multiple tasks. We evaluate various baseline methods with and without large-scale VidL pre-training, and systematically investigate the impact of video input channels, fusion methods, and different video representations. We also study the transferability between tasks, and conduct multi-task learning under different settings. The significant gap between our best model and human performance calls for future study for advanced VidL models. VALUE is available at https://value-benchmark.github.io/.
evaluation_method: Task-specific metrics (Recall@K / mAP for retrieval, accuracy for VQA, BLEU/METEOR/CIDEr for captioning)
general_score_metric: Task-specific (Recall@K for retrieval; Accuracy for VQA; CIDEr/BLEU/METEOR for captioning)
typical_sota_score: Varies by task and dataset subset (example ranges): retrieval R@1 ~30–60%; VQA accuracy ~45–75%; captioning CIDEr ~25–50
reputation: Moderately adopted as a multi-task video-and-language benchmark for research into cross-task transfer and multimodal pretraining, though not as widely used as some single-task datasets.
notes: Heterogeneous tasks and metrics complicate direct comparisons; includes subtitles which may not always be available; potential overlap/contamination from large pretraining corpora; useful for multi-task evaluation rather than single-metric saturation.
